claims.nodeLabel: STAR GATE and predecessor remote viewing programs, 1970-1995
claims.sourceText: Wikipedia, Stargate Project (U.S. Army unit), citing declassified programme records — DEMOTED from Tier 1 (cited to a secondary/encyclopedic source); needs primary replacement
claims.text: The programme ran under successive cryptonyms: SCANATE (c.1970, CIA), GONDOLA WISH (1977, Army ACSI SED), GRILL FLAME (mid-1978, INSCOM, Fort Meade Buildings 2560-2561), CENTER LANE (1983), SUN STREAK (late 1985, DIA S&TI), STAR GATE (1991).

b.label: STAR GATE and predecessor remote viewing programs, 1970-1995

edges.label: Both are demonstrations of decades-long concealment ending in bulk declassification
edges.note: Groom Lake ran 58 years to specific acknowledgement via FOIA; STAR GATE ran 25 years to bulk CREST publication in 2017. Reasoning: structural comparison of two documented concealment lifecycles.

b.label: STAR GATE and predecessor remote viewing programs, 1970-1995

edges.label: Puthoff was principal investigator and project director
edges.note: Puthoff co-founded the SRI programme with Targ and directed the research phase before leaving in the mid-1980s.

b.label: STAR GATE and predecessor remote viewing programs, 1970-1995

edges.label: Ran the SRI International half of the government's psychoenergetics effort
edges.note: The same principal investigator ran the SRI remote viewing science, produced Defense Intelligence Reference Documents under AAWSAP, and co-founded To The Stars Academy, which signed the CRADA with the Army in 2019. Reasoning: continuity of a single documented career, not of a single programme.

b.label: STAR GATE and predecessor remote viewing programs, 1970-1995

edges.label: Clapper led the programme in the 1990s before becoming DNI
edges.note: Clapper is recorded as a project leader in the 1990s; he later served as Director of National Intelligence.

b.label: STAR GATE and predecessor remote viewing programs, 1970-1995

edges.label: Targ co-founded the SRI remote viewing research
edges.note: Targ collaborated with Puthoff on the early SRI work and on the tests with Geller, Swann and Price.

a.label: STAR GATE and predecessor remote viewing programs, 1970-1995

edges.label: Green ran the CIA analytic side of the anomalous-phenomena portfolio
edges.note: Green's CIA Life Sciences work on anomalous phenomena is the analytic counterpart to the SRI research, and his later Wayne State position carried the biomedical line into NIDS/BAASS and the modern Stanford circle. Reasoning: continuity of documented affiliations, not of a single programme.

a.label: STAR GATE and predecessor remote viewing programs, 1970-1995

edges.label: DIA held the programme from 1985 as SUN STREAK and STAR GATE
edges.note: The effort moved to DIA's Scientific and Technical Intelligence Directorate as SUN STREAK in late 1985 and was consolidated as STAR GATE in 1991.

a.label: STAR GATE and predecessor remote viewing programs, 1970-1995

edges.label: SRI held the science half of the remote viewing effort from 1972
edges.note: Puthoff and Targ began CIA-sponsored work at SRI's Artificial Intelligence Center in 1972 and continued with intelligence community funding until they left in the mid-1980s.
